Classifier for All\sphinxhyphen{}Positive Bags using Axis\sphinxhyphen{}Aligned Positive Region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This classifier assigns a positive label to bags that contain instances within a predefined
axis\sphinxhyphen{}parallel rectangle (APR) defined by the minimum and maximum feature values of positive
instances in the training set.

Calculate the pairwise distance matrix between bags.

Only the upper triangular part is calculated explicitly.

\section{Maximal Hausdorff}
\label{\detokenize{core/index:maximal-hausdorff}}\index{MaximalHausdorff (class in miml.core.maximal\_hausdorff)@\spxentry{MaximalHausdorff}\spxextra{class in miml.core.maximal\_hausdorff}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: {\hyperref[\detokenize{core/index:miml.core.hausdorff_distance.HausdorffDistance}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HausdorffDistance}}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Directed Hausdorff distance from the first bag to the second.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For every instance in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bag1}}, the distance to its closest instance
in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bag2}} is calculated. The maximum of these minimum distances
is returned.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a directed distance, meaning that:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distance(bag1, bag2)}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
is not necessarily equal to:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distance(bag2, bag1)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Bidirectional Average Hausdorff distance between two bags.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The distance is calculated by finding the closest instance in the
other bag for every instance in each direction. The resulting
distances are averaged and then normalized to the range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}0, 1)}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A small positive value is returned instead of zero to improve
numerical stability in algorithms that use the distance as a
denominator.
